problem:
By integrating first with respect to $x,$ then $y,$ and then $z,$ evaluate the triple integral 

$$
{∭}_{R}2x+3{y}^{2}+4{z}^{3}\,dV
$$

over the rectangular box $R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 3,\,0\le y\le 2,\,0\le z\le 1}.$

feedback.problem:
By integrating first with respect to $y,$ then $z,$ and then $x,$ evaluate the triple integral 

$$
{∭}_{R}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y+z)\,dV
$$

over the rectangular box $R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le \frac{\pi }{2},\,0\le y\le \pi ,\,0\le z\le \pi }.$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we express our triple integral as a repeated integral:

$$
{∭}_{R}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y+z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y+z)\,dy\,dz\,dx
$$

Since we're integrating first with respect to $y,$ then $z,$ and then $x,$ we write $\text{d}V=\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x.$

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $y,$ treating $x$ and $z$ as constants: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y+z)\,dy\,dz\,dx & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }[{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y+z)\,dy]dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }[-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+y+z)]_{0}^{\pi }\,dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+z+\pi )+\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+z+0)\,dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+z)+\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+z)\,dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }2\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+z)\,dz\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $z,$ treating $x$ as a constant: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }2\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+z)\,dz\,dx & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}[{\int }_{0}^{\pi }2\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+z)\,dz]dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}2[\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+z)]_{z=0}^{z=\pi }\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}2(\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+\pi )-\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+0))\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}2(-\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\operatorname{sin}⁡x)\,dx \\  & =-4{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-4{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,dx & =4[\operatorname{cos}⁡x]_{x=0}^{x=\pi /2} \\  & =4(0-1) \\  & =-4\end{aligned}
$$
